title: Decisions inside a Tauri window-event handler must live in a function a test can call
rule: When a Builder::on_window_event (or Window::on_window_event) closure decides something a criterion depends on (prevent_close on CloseRequested, hide instead of quit), put the whole decision, including the call that acts on it, in a pub function that takes the window and a callback (e.g. `on_close_requested(window, || api.prevent_close())`), and keep the closure a single non-branching line. Tauri's MockRuntime drops window-event listeners (tauri test/mock_runtime.rs on_window_event is a no-op), so a test cannot reach the closure itself. Test the function with a recording callback and assert both that it is called and that it is not.
rationale: E17.1 (#126): the close closure in lib.rs called api.prevent_close() after the tested decision function returned; deleting that call or inverting the check would have quit the app on close and dropped session fonts with every test green.
